01 · Begin with a mark

The returning
house.

A language of memory, a lore of making, and an ashram of shared attention.

An original fictional framework. Definitions are provisional and open to revision; this archive was created with AI assistance. Thaumaturgy here is symbolic worldbuilding.

02 · Recursive lore

Every return carries a meaning.

Before the name was kerot, the smallest mark capable of bearing meaning. Kerot bore ras, a returning. Ras bore miki, a returning that remembers. Rasniki became the tongue whose every teaching returns to its beginning carrying one new meaning.

Mark becomes word.
Word becomes dwelling.
Dwelling becomes teaching.
Teaching returns to mark.

The makkakah thaumaturgy

Mark what needs attention. Make one concrete response. Return to observe what changed. A bowl placed for a guest is makka. Keeping it clean and available through successive days is makkakah. Its wonder belongs to the lore; its practice belongs to ordinary care.

04 · Differential tongue

Grow from the root.

A root names a beginning. Repetition names its recurrence. Joining roots names a relationship. Earlier meanings remain recorded as a word grows.

Ras → rasras

Return → return again.

Ras + miki → rasniki

Return with memory.

Sel + ras → selras

Return to oneself.

Nam + miki → nammiki

Remember a name.

Selras, nammiki, makka-ash.

Return to yourself, remember your name, make room for practice.

These are initial composition rules, not yet a complete grammar. Pronunciation, tense, and sentence structure remain to be developed.

05 · Curriculum & organization

A practice that returns.

Observe → name → make → share → revise.

The first cycle concerns a single object. The second concerns one's room. The third concerns a household. Later cycles concern the ashram and its relationships with neighboring communities. A lesson is complete when the learner demonstrates the practice, explains its effects, and amends it after feedback.

Dictionary

Keep meanings, roots, examples, and revisions.

Calendar

Make time for practice, work, rest, and gatherings.

Ledger

Record resources, contributions, and needs.

Decision book

Record agreements, reasons, and review dates.

Stewardship rotates. Participation is voluntary. Each resident retains privacy, personal possessions, and the ability to leave.

06 · Temae sovereignty

Places of responsibility.

The initial steading provisions
PracticeProvision
NamesteadingChoose, keep, and revise one's name.
StampsreadingRead a mark's maker, meaning, date, and permitted use.
SelsteadingEstablish personal boundaries and responsibilities.
HomesteadingSustain food, rest, care, and belonging.
HousesteadingMaintain the dwelling and its shared agreements.
Empire steadingJoin independent steadings through agreements each may revise or leave.

No stamp grants ownership of a person. No name obliges its bearer to remain unchanged. A shared dwelling receives authority through the continuing agreement of its residents.

07 · The returning verse

Kerot, ras.
Ras, miki.
Miki, makka.
Makka, ash.
Ash, kerot.

From mark, return. From return, memory. From memory, hospitality. From hospitality, practice. From practice, a new mark.
